title: Serum soluble (s)Axl assay protocol
author: Ioannis Parodis
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.wnnfdde
materials: SERUM SOLUBLE (S)AXL ASSAY PROTOCOL MATERIALS AND TOOLS BD	Vacutainer	tubes	(Catalogue	number:	367812) Immulon®	2	HB	Flat	Bottom	MicroTiter®	Plate Microplate	reader:	ELX808	from	BioTek	Instruments	(Winooski,	VT) Human	Axl	ELISA	kit	(Catalogue	number:	DY154)	(R&D	Systems) • PBS: 137 mM NaCl, 2.7 mM KCl,	8.1 mM Na2HPO4, 1.5 mM KH2PO4,	pH 7.2-7.4, 0.2 μm	filtered	(R&D	Systems;	Catalogue	number:	DY006).	• Wash	Buffer:	0.05%	Tween®	20	in	PBS,	pH	7.2-7.4	(R&D	Systems®,	Catalogue	number:	WA126).	• Reagent Diluent: 1% BSA (bovine serum albumin)	in PBS, pH 7.2-7.4, 0.2	μm filtered (R&D	Systems,	Catalogue	number:	DY995). • Substrate Solution: 1:1 mixture of Color Reagent A (H2O2) and Color Reagent B	(Tetramethylbenzidine)	(R&D	Systems,	Catalogue	number:	DY999).	• Stop	Solution:	2	N	H2SO4	(R&D	Systems,	Catalogue	number:	DY994). SERUM COLLECTION AND STORAGE 1. Whole	blood	was	collected	into	BD	Vacutainer	tubes	without	any	additives	(Catalogue	number:	367812). 2. After	20	minutes	of	incubation	at	room	temperature,	the	tubes	were	centrifuged	10	minutes	at	3,000	rpm	at	room	temperature. 3. The	supernatant	was	carefully	separated	and	aliquoted	into	100	μL	aliquots	and	stored	at	-80°C	prior	to	batch	processing.

steps.title: Coat Microplate
steps.instruction: Dilute the Capture Antibody to the working concentration in PBS without carrier protein and coat a 96-well microplate (Immulon® 2 HB flat bottom).

substeps.instruction: Add 50 μL of diluted Capture Antibody per well.
Seal the plate and incubate overnight at room temperature.

steps.title: Wash Plate
steps.instruction: Aspirate each well and wash the plate three times with Wash Buffer.

substeps.instruction: Fill each well with 300 μL Wash Buffer using a squirt bottle, manifold dispenser, or plate washer.
Completely remove residual liquid at the final step by tapping the inverted plate against paper towels.

steps.title: Block Plate
steps.instruction: Block the plates by adding 200 μL Reagent Diluent to each well and incubate at room temperature for 1.5 hours.

steps.title: Prepare Samples and Standards
steps.instruction: Prepare samples and standards during the blocking period.

substeps.instruction: Dilute serum samples 1:50 in Reagent Diluent (ensure enough for two wells at 50 μL per well).
Prepare a seven-point standard curve using 2-fold serial dilutions in reagent diluent, with the highest concentration at 4000 pg/mL.

steps.title: Add Samples and Standards
steps.instruction: Wash the plate (as per the Wash Plate step), then add 50 μL of samples or standards in Reagent Diluent per well in duplicate.

substeps.instruction: Cover with an adhesive strip and incubate for 2 hours at room temperature.

steps.title: Add Detection Antibody
steps.instruction: Wash the plate (as per the Wash Plate step), then add 50 μL of Detection Antibody diluted in Reagent Diluent to each well.

substeps.instruction: Cover with a new adhesive strip and incubate for 2 hours at room temperature.

steps.title: Add Streptavidin-HRP
steps.instruction: Wash the plate (as per the Wash Plate step), then add 50 μL of the working dilution of Streptavidin-HRP A to each well.

substeps.instruction: Cover the plate and incubate for 20 minutes at room temperature.
Wrap the plate with aluminum foil to protect from direct light.

steps.title: Develop Signal
steps.instruction: Wash the plate (as per the Wash Plate step), then add 50 μL of Substrate Solution to each well.

substeps.instruction: Incubate for 20 minutes at room temperature.
Wrap the plate with aluminum foil to protect from direct light.

steps.title: Stop Reaction and Read
steps.instruction: Stop the reaction and measure the optical density.

substeps.instruction: Add 25 μL of Stop Solution to each well and gently tap the plate to mix.
Immediately determine the optical density of each well using a microplate reader set to 450 nm.

steps.title: Calculate Concentration
steps.instruction: Calculate the Axl concentration based on the generated standard curve.
